chunks.text: The Sun's storms don't stay up in the sky.
In March nineteen eighty-nine, one reached down to Quebec, and the province's power grid collapsed in about ninety seconds.
The lights stayed off for about nine hours.
Today, more than ten thousand Starlink satellites are circling the planet, and a storm doesn't need to be big to bring new ones down.
So somebody has to tell us, years ahead, how wild the Sun is going to get.
The Sun is about as quiet as it ever gets, its face almost bare.
And a panel of experts is weighing nearly fifty different ways to guess what it'll do next.
